aldemar.headline: Palantir is three-quarters of a per cent from its stop — and CPI prints at 08:30
aldemar.standfirst: Citigroup cut Palantir to Market Perform on valuation and the stock closed 165.86, 0.85% above its stop, on volume 54% below average. That is a position at its line rather than near it, and an ordinary session resolves it. Around it the tape deteriorated for a fourth straight day: the S&P fell 0.58% to 7,591.70 and closed below its 50-day for the first time in this sequence, WTI settled at $102.48 with Saudi production reported at its lowest since 1990, the ten-year rose 11bp to 4.94% and the thirty-year to its highest since June 2007, and net gamma deepened again to −$44.19B. One thing went right: AAPL rose 3.56% after Deepwater doubled its iPhone Duo revenue estimate, turning the position green. Heat 3.15R against 3.0R.

positions.title: Palantir is at its stop, Apple turned green, and the two are the whole story.

items.html: BAC — Flat while the long end broke to 2007 levels. BAC slipped 0.18% on a session when the ten-year rose 11bp to 4.94% and the thirty-year reached its highest since June 2007. No company news. The thesis said a bank should benefit from higher-for-longer; four sessions of the steepest rate moves of the year have produced −0.46R. At some point that stops being patience and starts being evidence.

PLTR — Citigroup cuts to Market Perform, and the stop is three-quarters of a per cent away. Citigroup downgraded Palantir from Buy to Market Perform and BTIG assigned Neutral, both on valuation at roughly 142 times earnings, against a consensus target of $192.19. The stock closed 165.86, down 2.2%, and it did so on 20.7m shares — 54% below the 45.1m average, which is a drift lower on no participation rather than a liquidation. Positive news was ignored: partnerships with NVIDIA and Fujitsu and a $127m Army contract, none of it yet in quantified guidance. A sell-side downgrade is a thesis event, and it lands with the stop 0.75% below the close — the position is at its line, not near it.

AAPL — Munster doubles his Duo revenue estimate and the position turns green. Gene Munster of Deepwater doubled his estimate of the iPhone Duo's share of fiscal 2027 iPhone revenue from 5% to 10%, and said March 2027 growth should be nearer 20% against the Street's 14%, on the split launch cycle. Morningstar lifted fair value to $290; Jefferies kept Underperform at $263.66, so the sell side is not united. The stock rose 3.56% to 326.57 — the best day of any position this month — taking it from −0.32R to green. A $1,999 tier being taken seriously on revenue rather than dismissed on price is the bull case arriving.

Signal changes the thesis, the levels or the size; everything else is filed as noise.

world.title: Oil through $100 on Saudi supply, the long end at 2007 levels, and CPI into both.

items.html: WTI settled at $102.48, up 6.69%, and Brent reached $107.63 — both above $100 for the first time since May. Saudi Arabia reported production at its lowest level since 1990, with Houthi strikes on energy facilities and the Hormuz disruption behind it; petrol is averaging $4.27 a gallon. This has stopped being a risk premium on a functioning market and become a supply number, which is a harder thing for a CPI print to look through.

The ten-year rose 11bp to 4.94%, the highest in nearly three years, and the thirty-year reached 5.35%, the highest since June 2007. Mortgage rates crossed 7% for the first time in over a year. The VIX broke to 17.84, up 17% on the week, after 28 sessions in a 14–17 range. A bond market moving like that the day before CPI is repricing, not positioning.

Phoenix's top eight is now four oil names and three marine shipping names — DK, PBR, BP and PSX alongside BWLP, DAC and NMM, with NMM, BP and PSX new since yesterday. The war has stopped being a macro input and become what the screener returns. Tanker rates are the cleanest expression of a strait barely passing ten ships a day.

world.note: The oil item and the shipping item are one fact from two ends. Crude feeds CPI, CPI is the gate holding the regime, and the print is this morning at 08:30 ET.

aldemar.ondeck: August CPI lands today, Friday 11 September at 08:30 ET, and is the regime's tightest gate; the Bank of Japan meets next week with a hike 97% priced; the FOMC meets 15–16 September; triple witching is 18 September. Tomorrow's brief covers the CPI session and carries the weekly.

This brief therefore has no Wednesday close, no Wednesday marks and no Wednesday R for any position. What follows in The World is sourced from the press and labelled as such.

Brent closed above $100 for the first time since July, up 3.4% on the day, with WTI at $95.39 and Treasury yields at fresh 52-week highs (TheStreet, KRMG). CPI prints this morning at 08:30 ET into that. Crude is the mechanism that moves the gate holding this regime.

Apple shipped the catalyst. The iPhone Duo foldable came in at $1,999 — under the $2,000-plus trailed — with pre-orders 16 October. The stock swung about 1.5%% off its lows to close roughly flat near $316. The event this position was carrying is now behind it.

markets.title: The index is sitting exactly on the gamma boundary, and it crossed to the wrong side.

items.html: SPX 7,591.70, -0.58% on the day, -0.16% above the 50-day and +6.07% above the 200-day — the 50-day cushion more than halved from 1.67% on Friday. VIX 17.84, +8.38% on the day.

Net gamma −$44.19B, regime negative, down from +$36.13B a session earlier. In negative gamma dealers hedge with the move — selling weakness, buying strength — so the same news produces a bigger index move than it would have last week. Distance to the flip is +0.66%: not near the boundary, on it, so a small rally switches the amplification off again.

On 4 and 7 September I called the sign of dist_to_flip_pct contradictory. Today's flip resolves it: the field is signed flip minus spot, so a negative distance means the flip sits below spot, which is what positive gamma is. The convention was right and I misread it. The sequence −0.92%, −0.36%, +0.04% was the cushion eroding for three packs before it crossed.
The flip level, call wall and put wall are all null, so none of the above can be pinned to a price. The market block's own dxy, us10y, gold and wti are null too while the macro block carries them.

markets.note: The risk sentence for the day is that distance: at 0.04% the index has no gamma cushion in either direction going into CPI.

macro.title: The long end broke to levels not seen since 2007, and crude is up nearly a quarter in a month.

items.html: The ten-year is 4.94%, +11bp on the day, +15bp on the week, +26bp on the month. The two-year is 4.43%. The 2s10s curve is 51bp and has flattened 5bp over the month — the opposite of last week, when it was 55bp and steepening. The real ten-year is 2.46%, +1bp on the week. A flattening curve with the front end higher is the market putting the Fed back in play, which is a different message from the one this section carried on Monday.

The ten-year series is now tracking daily — +11bp on the day is the first real daily move it has shown. us02, real10 and hy are not: all three read 0bp on the day for a fourth session, and hy is still quoted in percent rather than basis points. Read the front end and credit at weekly resolution. Bitcoin is also carrying an identical level and change to yesterday's pack, which suggests it is being held rather than refreshed.

The dollar index is 99.09, +0.32% on the day and -0.47% on the week — easing, not tightening. The yen is the one that matters and Phoenix now tracks it: macro.absent is empty for the first time and USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week. Four per cent in a week is snapping, not drifting. Markets put 97% odds on a BoJ hike next week against 52% a month ago, on a record ¥360tn ($2.35tn) of cross-border yen borrowing, with three-month implied vol at a six-month high. This is the carry trade's funding leg repricing before the hike lands.

High yield at 268bp once the unit switch is undone, flat on the week and flat on the month — comfortably inside the 300bp line that separates calm from watchful. Credit is not worried, and that is real information: it is why the cyclical side of this book still gets the benefit of the doubt.

Gold 4,364.50, -1.17% on the day and only -0.42% on the month — it has stopped being the war hedge. Bitcoin 78,260, -0.23% on the day but +22.45% on the month, which is not yet what a liquidity squeeze looks like. Crude is the one feeding the gate: 102.48, +6.69% on the day, +12.60% on the week and +23.17% on the month, with CPI at 3.3 against a 2.5 threshold and printing Friday. A fifth on the oil price in a month is the whole inflation argument in one number.

WTI 102.48, +6.69% on the day, +12.60% on the week and +23.17% on the month — through $100 for the first time since May, with Saudi production reported at its lowest since 1990. Gold fell -1.17% to 4,364.50 and bitcoin was flat, so this is not a fear bid: it is a supply shock being priced into the inflation path, with CPI at 3.3 against a 2.5 threshold and printing this morning.

The Fed and the data have stopped disagreeing. Waller leaned toward holding on 3 September and the market rallied; payrolls at 162,000 argued back on the 4th; by Tuesday traders priced roughly 60% odds of a hike at the 15–16 September meeting, against the 54/46 coin flip after Waller spoke. The data and the oil price now pull the same way.

macro.note: The gates. Three of four hold. CPI y/y at 3.3 clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.8; the real ten-year's three-month change at 33bp now clears by 8bp, having been 3bp clear on Monday — that gate moved away from flipping, not toward it; drawdown clears by 9.51. The two-year's three-month change at 29bp against 40bp still fails. Runner-up is ENERGY_GRIND, one gate short: it needs the three-month CPI change above 0.3 and sits at −0.16.

invalidation.title: One resolves at 08:30. One resolves on almost any down day.

items.html: PLTR closes below 164.45. It is 0.85% away. On a name whose daily range averages well over that, this resolves on an ordinary session, and it would take heat from 3.15R to roughly 2.15R without a decision being made. The question worth answering before the open is whether you want the stop to make it.

August CPI at 08:30 ET prints at or below 3.0% year over year. The gate's cushion falls from 0.8 to 0.5 or less. Note the asymmetry: with WTI at 102.48 and hike odds near 70%, the market is positioned for a hard print, so a soft one lands in a crowded trade — and at −$44.19B of gamma the reaction is multiplied either way.

The Bank of Japan hikes next week and USDJPY breaks below 150. It is 153.57, -4.13% on the week, and 97% priced. A disorderly unwind of a record ¥360tn carry position damages this book without any position's thesis being wrong, and at this gamma depth the index amplifies it.

weekly.headline: A week that changed everything and moved nothing — the S&P finished nine basis points higher
weekly.standfirst: Between Monday and Friday the US turned a single retaliatory strike into a naval campaign, escorted 18 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz in a day, struck Iranian oil tankers, and had ballistic missiles fired at an aircraft carrier. Three Fed speakers moved September from a near-certain hike to a coin flip and payrolls then printed at three times consensus. WTI added 9.69% to 91.48 and the 10-year rose to 4.78%. The S&P 500 closed the week at 7,718.60, up 0.09%. Everything that happened, happened underneath: PLTR fell 6.42% through a 22-point range on a competitive threat from Alphabet, GOOG fell 2.14% while Berkshire's $37.8bn stake purchase came to light, BAC gained 1.10% on the wrong days, and AAPL round-tripped a CEO handover into a bad product leak five days before its event.

3 positions open into the weekend, -0.3R of open risk in aggregate, against an S&P that moved +0.09% on the week. The percentage column is the week for names held into it and entry-to-date for names opened inside it; the last column is always against entry.

Five sessions, one flat index, and a book that moved in four directions

TAPES&P +0.09% on the week to 7,718.60 — flat through a war escalation, a four-way Fed split and a blowout payroll print. Monday's oil shock, Tuesday's strike campaign, Wednesday's Williams relief, Thursday's Waller dovishness and Friday's 162,000 payrolls netted to nine basis points. WTI added 9.69% to 91.48 and the 10-year rose to 4.78%; the index absorbed both. When a week that eventful goes nowhere, the information is in the dispersion, not the level.Phoenix engine · 2026-09-04
PLTRPLTR −6.42% on the week — the worst position, and the only one whose thesis changed. Range 165.71 to 187.94 in five sessions. Alphabet's Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber release under the government-only Fairwind programme took 5.81% out of it on Wednesday; a PwC partnership took 7.71% back on Thursday; Friday gave up another 4.5%. The momentum entry that justified the position no longer exists and the competitive question is unresolved. It has no stop and is not in trades.json.Investing.com · Benzinga · Phoenix engine · 2026-09-04
FEDThree Fed speakers in three days moved September from ~62% to a coin flip and back toward a hike. Williams tied the yield surge to a strong economy, Waller said he would support holding, then payrolls printed at three times consensus and two-year yields closed at a 52-week high. Chair Warsh remains hawkish and Hammack says now is the time to act. The committee is split four ways and CPI on 11 September is the tiebreak.Bond Buyer · FXStreet · TheStreet · 2026-09-04
GOOGGOOG −2.14% on the week to 335.31, but 0.83R to 0.47R is the number that matters. Alphabet entered defence AI, moved a competitor 7%, and finished the week down. Berkshire added $37.8bn of GOOGL and TCI $4.4bn in the June quarter, which is the strongest positioning confirmation anywhere in the pack. The FTC's YouTube suit is still unfiled and still live.Phoenix fact pack · IBKR · 2026-09-04
BACBAC +1.10% on the week — the only position that gained, and it gained on the dovish days. −0.60R to −0.43R for Gabriel, −0.48R to −0.33R for Aldemar. Three consecutive gains mid-week came while the September hike case was weakening, not strengthening, which is the opposite of the thesis. Friday's hot payrolls should have been the best day of the week for it and the stock closed 0.06% lower.Phoenix engine · 2026-09-04
AAPLAAPL +0.08% on the week — a round trip through the CEO handover into a bad product leak. Ternus took over on 1 September and the stock gained 2.61%; it held the gap for three sessions and then fell 2.51% on Friday after reports the foldable iPhone is being produced at low volumes and Omdia said two MacBooks were cancelled. The event is 9 September. No stop, and not in trades.json.Motley Fool · MacRumors/Omdia · Phoenix engine · 2026-09-04

Four positions, four different weeks, and an index that did nothing. The book's problem is not direction, it is that heat is 3.16R against a 3.0R cap while two of the five names are invisible to the engine entirely.

sections.right: campaign · warships targeted · tankers struck · WTI +9.69% on the week
sections.html:
From one strike to a naval campaign in five sessions

strikeUS strikes escalate from two launchers at Larak to ~60 installations around the strait, then to Iranian oil tankers. Monday's action followed two Saudi supertankers being hit; Tuesday brought strikes at Qeshm Island, Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Jask and Sirik; by the weekend the US had disabled two Iranian crude carriers and destroyed a third near Kharg Island, which CENTCOM said financed the IRGC and its proxies.2026-08-31 to 09-05
militaryThe IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. Both evaded, no personnel hurt. Iran's earlier retaliation — missiles at Jordan, drones at Bahrain and Kuwait — was intercepted in full twice. Iran warned of "a significant response" and Trump said the US may target Pickaxe Mountain "very soon", returning to the nuclear file after a week of shipping lanes.2026-09-05
oilWTI +9.69% on the week to 91.48 — and it fell on the two days the war escalated most. The US escorted 40 vessels carrying 18 million barrels through the strait in a single day, close to pre-conflict throughput. Charter rates above $500,000 a day and record diesel prices say the commercial market is less convinced than the futures curve.2026-09-04
talksTrump closes the off-ramp: "an agreement with them isn't worth the paper it's written on". Pezeshkian had spent the week offering to honour the June memorandum, which includes free navigation, if the US reciprocated. That is the fastest path to unwinding the crude premium and it is now rhetorically shut.2026-09-03

The week's lesson is that the transmission broke. Crude rose 9.69% and the S&P finished flat; missiles hit at a carrier and crude fell. Waller made September about CPI rather than oil, so a barrel no longer converts into a rate hike. That holds until an escorted convoy is successfully attacked — the one event that would reprice insurance, freight and the inflation path at once.

A closed Monday, a product event, and the print that decides the meeting

CPICPI release — 08:30 ET. The regime's tightest gate is CPI y/y.in 5 days2026-09-11
FOMCFOMC decision — Rate decision 14:00 ET, press conference 14:30in 10 days2026-09-16
OPEXTriple witching — Index, options and futures expire together; the largest positioning reset of the quarter.in 12 days2026-09-18
CLOSEDLabor Day, Monday 7 September. US markets closed. Three days of war headlines with no way to trade them.Mon
EVENTApple product event, Wednesday 9 September. A foldable iPhone is the expected headline and the week ended with a report that it is being produced at low volumes. The position has no stop.Wed
CPIAugust CPI, Friday 11 September, 08:30 ET. The regime's tightest gate and, after Waller, the tiebreak for the 16 September meeting. A print at or below 3.0% y/y is the first real argument against POLICY_TIGHTENING.Fri
BOOKHeat is 3.16R against a 3.0R cap. Nothing from a 700-name screener is actionable until that is back under the cap. Adding PLTR and AAPL to trades.json with stops fixes the heat number and the R math in one edit.before Tue

Two dated catalysts and one housekeeping job. The housekeeping is the one that changes what you can do.

Apple shipped the catalyst. The iPhone Duo foldable came in at $1,999 — under the $2,000-plus trailed — with pre-orders 16 October. The stock swung about 1.5%% off its lows to close roughly flat near $316. The event this position was carrying is now behind it.

markets.title: The index is sitting exactly on the gamma boundary, and it crossed to the wrong side.

items.html: SPX 7,591.70, -0.58% on the day, -0.16% above the 50-day and +6.07% above the 200-day — the 50-day cushion more than halved from 1.67% on Friday. VIX 17.84, +8.38% on the day.

Net gamma −$44.19B, regime negative, down from +$36.13B a session earlier. In negative gamma dealers hedge with the move — selling weakness, buying strength — so the same news produces a bigger index move than it would have last week. Distance to the flip is +0.66%: not near the boundary, on it, so a small rally switches the amplification off again.

On 4 and 7 September I called the sign of dist_to_flip_pct contradictory. Today's flip resolves it: the field is signed flip minus spot, so a negative distance means the flip sits below spot, which is what positive gamma is. The convention was right and I misread it. The sequence −0.92%, −0.36%, +0.04% was the cushion eroding for three packs before it crossed.
The flip level, call wall and put wall are all null, so none of the above can be pinned to a price. The market block's own dxy, us10y, gold and wti are null too while the macro block carries them.

markets.note: The risk sentence for the day is that distance: at 0.04% the index has no gamma cushion in either direction going into CPI.

macro.title: The long end broke to levels not seen since 2007, and crude is up nearly a quarter in a month.

items.html: The ten-year is 4.94%, +11bp on the day, +15bp on the week, +26bp on the month. The two-year is 4.43%. The 2s10s curve is 51bp and has flattened 5bp over the month — the opposite of last week, when it was 55bp and steepening. The real ten-year is 2.46%, +1bp on the week. A flattening curve with the front end higher is the market putting the Fed back in play, which is a different message from the one this section carried on Monday.

The ten-year series is now tracking daily — +11bp on the day is the first real daily move it has shown. us02, real10 and hy are not: all three read 0bp on the day for a fourth session, and hy is still quoted in percent rather than basis points. Read the front end and credit at weekly resolution. Bitcoin is also carrying an identical level and change to yesterday's pack, which suggests it is being held rather than refreshed.

The dollar index is 99.09, +0.32% on the day and -0.47% on the week — easing, not tightening. The yen is the one that matters and Phoenix now tracks it: macro.absent is empty for the first time and USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week. Four per cent in a week is snapping, not drifting. Markets put 97% odds on a BoJ hike next week against 52% a month ago, on a record ¥360tn ($2.35tn) of cross-border yen borrowing, with three-month implied vol at a six-month high. This is the carry trade's funding leg repricing before the hike lands.

High yield at 268bp once the unit switch is undone, flat on the week and flat on the month — comfortably inside the 300bp line that separates calm from watchful. Credit is not worried, and that is real information: it is why the cyclical side of this book still gets the benefit of the doubt.

Gold 4,364.50, -1.17% on the day and only -0.42% on the month — it has stopped being the war hedge. Bitcoin 78,260, -0.23% on the day but +22.45% on the month, which is not yet what a liquidity squeeze looks like. Crude is the one feeding the gate: 102.48, +6.69% on the day, +12.60% on the week and +23.17% on the month, with CPI at 3.3 against a 2.5 threshold and printing Friday. A fifth on the oil price in a month is the whole inflation argument in one number.

WTI 102.48, +6.69% on the day, +12.60% on the week and +23.17% on the month — through $100 for the first time since May, with Saudi production reported at its lowest since 1990. Gold fell -1.17% to 4,364.50 and bitcoin was flat, so this is not a fear bid: it is a supply shock being priced into the inflation path, with CPI at 3.3 against a 2.5 threshold and printing this morning.

The Fed and the data have stopped disagreeing. Waller leaned toward holding on 3 September and the market rallied; payrolls at 162,000 argued back on the 4th; by Tuesday traders priced roughly 60% odds of a hike at the 15–16 September meeting, against the 54/46 coin flip after Waller spoke. The data and the oil price now pull the same way.

macro.note: The gates. Three of four hold. CPI y/y at 3.3 clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.8; the real ten-year's three-month change at 33bp now clears by 8bp, having been 3bp clear on Monday — that gate moved away from flipping, not toward it; drawdown clears by 9.51. The two-year's three-month change at 29bp against 40bp still fails. Runner-up is ENERGY_GRIND, one gate short: it needs the three-month CPI change above 0.3 and sits at −0.16.

Note the asymmetry: with WTI at 102.48 and hike odds near 70%, the market is positioned for a hard print, so a soft one lands in a crowded trade — and at −$44.19B of gamma the reaction is multiplied either way.

The Bank of Japan hikes next week and USDJPY breaks below 150. It is 153.57, -4.13% on the week, and 97% priced. A disorderly unwind of a record ¥360tn carry position damages this book without any position's thesis being wrong, and at this gamma depth the index amplifies it.

weekly.headline: A week that changed everything and moved nothing — the S&P finished nine basis points higher
weekly.standfirst: Between Monday and Friday the US turned a single retaliatory strike into a naval campaign, escorted 18 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz in a day, struck Iranian oil tankers, and had ballistic missiles fired at an aircraft carrier. Three Fed speakers moved September from a near-certain hike to a coin flip and payrolls then printed at three times consensus. WTI added 9.69% to 91.48 and the 10-year rose to 4.78%. The S&P 500 closed the week at 7,718.60, up 0.09%. Everything that happened, happened underneath: PLTR fell 6.42% through a 22-point range on a competitive threat from Alphabet, GOOG fell 2.14% while Berkshire's $37.8bn stake purchase came to light, BAC gained 1.10% on the wrong days, and AAPL round-tripped a CEO handover into a bad product leak five days before its event.

sections.right: campaign · warships targeted · tankers struck · WTI +9.69% on the week
sections.html:
From one strike to a naval campaign in five sessions

strikeUS strikes escalate from two launchers at Larak to ~60 installations around the strait, then to Iranian oil tankers. Monday's action followed two Saudi supertankers being hit; Tuesday brought strikes at Qeshm Island, Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Jask and Sirik; by the weekend the US had disabled two Iranian crude carriers and destroyed a third near Kharg Island, which CENTCOM said financed the IRGC and its proxies.2026-08-31 to 09-05
militaryThe IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. Both evaded, no personnel hurt. Iran's earlier retaliation — missiles at Jordan, drones at Bahrain and Kuwait — was intercepted in full twice. Iran warned of "a significant response" and Trump said the US may target Pickaxe Mountain "very soon", returning to the nuclear file after a week of shipping lanes.2026-09-05
oilWTI +9.69% on the week to 91.48 — and it fell on the two days the war escalated most. The US escorted 40 vessels carrying 18 million barrels through the strait in a single day, close to pre-conflict throughput. Charter rates above $500,000 a day and record diesel prices say the commercial market is less convinced than the futures curve.2026-09-04
talksTrump closes the off-ramp: "an agreement with them isn't worth the paper it's written on". Pezeshkian had spent the week offering to honour the June memorandum, which includes free navigation, if the US reciprocated. That is the fastest path to unwinding the crude premium and it is now rhetorically shut.2026-09-03

The week's lesson is that the transmission broke. Crude rose 9.69% and the S&P finished flat; missiles hit at a carrier and crude fell. Waller made September about CPI rather than oil, so a barrel no longer converts into a rate hike. That holds until an escorted convoy is successfully attacked — the one event that would reprice insurance, freight and the inflation path at once.
